207	    def handover(self, source_assignee, assignees, reason, transferred_at, max_open=5):
208	        source_assignee = text(source_assignee, "source_assignee")
209	        reason = text(reason, "reason")
210	        if not isinstance(assignees, list) or not assignees:
211	            raise ValueError("assignees must be a nonempty array")
212	        names = []
213	        for element in assignees:
214	            if not isinstance(element, str) or not element.strip():
215	                raise ValueError("assignees elements must be nonblank strings")
216	            names.append(element.strip())
217	        if len(set(names)) != len(names):
218	            raise ValueError("assignees must not contain duplicate names")
219	        if source_assignee in names:
220	            raise ValueError("assignees must not contain the source assignee")
221	        transferred_at = minute(transferred_at, "transferred_at")
222	        max_open = positive(max_open, "max_open")
223	        data = self._read()
224	        tickets = data.get("tickets", {})
225	        def candidate_key(ticket):
226	            opened_at = ticket.get("opened_at")
227	            return (PRIORITY_RANK[ticket.get("priority", "normal")],
228	                    opened_at is None, opened_at if opened_at is not None else 0,
229	                    ticket["ticket_id"])
230	        selected = sorted((ticket for ticket in tickets.values()
231	                           if ticket["status"] == "open" and ticket.get("assignee") == source_assignee),
232	                          key=candidate_key)
233	        if not selected:
234	            return []
235	        loads = {name: 0 for name in names}
236	        for ticket in tickets.values():
237	            if ticket["status"] == "open" and ticket.get("assignee") in loads:
238	                loads[ticket["assignee"]] += 1
239	        plan = []
240	        for ticket in selected:
241	            available = [name for name in names if loads[name] < max_open]
242	            if not available:
243	                raise ValueError("assignees do not have enough capacity for all selected tickets")
244	            chosen = min(available, key=lambda name: (loads[name], name))
245	            loads[chosen] += 1
246	            plan.append((ticket, chosen))
247	        for ticket, chosen in plan:
248	            if "opened_at" in ticket and transferred_at < ticket["opened_at"]:
249	                raise ValueError("transferred_at must not be earlier than opened_at")
250	            history = ticket.get("transfer_history")
251	            if history and transferred_at < history[-1]["transferred_at"]:
252	                raise ValueError("transferred_at must not be earlier than the last transfer")
253	        handed_over = []
254	        for ticket, chosen in plan:
255	            ticket.setdefault("transfer_history", []).append(
256	                {"from_assignee": ticket["assignee"], "to_assignee": chosen,
257	                 "reason": reason, "transferred_at": transferred_at})
258	            ticket["assignee"] = chosen
259	            handed_over.append(ticket)
260	        self._write(data)
261	        return handed_over

270	            closed_at = minute(closed_at, "closed_at")
271	        def apply(ticket):
272	            if not ticket["assignee"]:

274	            if closed_at is not None:
275	                earlier = []
276	                if "opened_at" in ticket:

281	                earlier.extend(reply["replied_at"] for reply in ticket.get("replies") or [])
282	                earlier.extend(message["received_at"] for message in ticket.get("customer_messages") or [])
283	                earlier.extend(entry["transferred_at"] for entry in ticket.get("transfer_history") or [])
284	                earlier.extend(entry["closed_at"] for entry in ticket.get("reopen_history") or []
285	                               if "closed_at" in entry)

293	    def reopen_ticket(self, ticket_id, reason):
294	        ticket_id, reason = text(ticket_id, "ticket_id"), text(reason, "reason")
295	        data = self._read()
296	        ticket = data.get("tickets", {}).get(ticket_id)

299	        record = {"reason": reason, "resolution": ticket["resolution"]}

326	    def escalate_overdue(self, as_of, response_minutes=30, customer_minutes=30):
327	        as_of = minute(as_of, "as_of")
328	        response_minutes = positive(response_minutes, "response_minutes")
329	        customer_minutes = positive(customer_minutes, "customer_minutes")
330	        data = self._read()
331	        selected = []
332	        # All time validation runs before any priority change, so a future
333	        # record rejects the whole call without leaving partial escalations.
334	        for ticket in data.get("tickets", {}).values():
335	            if ticket["status"] != "open":
336	                continue
337	            response = ticket.get("first_response")
338	            has_response = isinstance(response, dict) and bool(response)
339	            if not has_response and "opened_at" in ticket:
340	                if ticket["opened_at"] > as_of:
341	                    raise ValueError("opened_at must not be later than as_of")
342	            messages = ticket.get("customer_messages")
343	            if messages:
344	                answer_times = ([response["responded_at"]] if has_response else [])
345	                answer_times.extend(reply["replied_at"] for reply in ticket.get("replies") or [])
346	                if any(message["received_at"] > as_of for message in messages) or \
347	                        any(time > as_of for time in answer_times):
348	                    raise ValueError("customer message or response time must not be later than as_of")
349	            overdue = False
350	            if not has_response:
351	                # Missing, null or an empty object means the ticket still awaits
352	                # its first response; tickets without opened_at do not take part.
353	                if "opened_at" in ticket and as_of - ticket["opened_at"] > response_minutes:
354	                    overdue = True
355	            if not overdue and messages:
356	                # The answer boundary is the latest of the first response and all
357	                # later replies; a follow-up in the same minute is already covered.
358	                boundary = max(answer_times) if answer_times else None
359	                unanswered = [message["received_at"] for message in messages
360	                              if boundary is None or message["received_at"] > boundary]
361	                if unanswered and as_of - min(unanswered) > customer_minutes:
362	                    overdue = True
363	            if overdue and ticket.get("priority") != "urgent":
364	                selected.append(ticket)

589	            if ticket["status"] != "open":

592	            # Only open tickets with a follow-up history participate.
593	            if not messages:
594	                continue
595	            response = ticket.get("first_response")
596	            # Missing, null or an empty object means there is no first response.
597	            response_at = response["responded_at"] if isinstance(response, dict) and response else None
598	            answer_times = ([response_at] if response_at is not None else [])
599	            answer_times.extend(reply["replied_at"] for reply in ticket.get("replies") or [])
600	            # Any follow-up or answer later than as_of invalidates the whole query.
601	            if any(message["received_at"] > as_of for message in messages) or \

604	            boundary = max(answer_times) if answer_times else None
605	            # A follow-up in the same minute as an answer is already covered;
606	            # only strictly later times remain unanswered.
607	            unanswered = [message for message in messages
608	                          if boundary is None or message["received_at"] > boundary]
609	            if not unanswered:
610	                continue
611	            earliest = min(message["received_at"] for message in unanswered)
612	            waiting = as_of - earliest

619	    def customer_response_report(self, as_of, since=0, until=None):
620	        # Parameters are validated even when the store holds no data.
621	        as_of = minute(as_of, "as_of")
622	        since = minute(since, "since")
623	        if until is not None:
624	            until = minute(until, "until")
625	            if until < since:
626	                raise ValueError("until must not be earlier than since")
627	        tickets = list(self._read().get("tickets", {}).values())
628	        # Only tickets with a follow-up history can contribute; open and closed tickets alike.
629	        participants = [ticket for ticket in tickets if ticket.get("customer_messages")]
630	        answers = {}
631	        windowed = {}
632	        for ticket in participants:
633	            # The window selects follow-ups by received time only: since is
634	            # inclusive, until exclusive and omitted/null means no upper bound;
635	            # equal bounds make the interval empty.
636	            pairs = [(index, message) for index, message in enumerate(ticket["customer_messages"])
637	                     if message["received_at"] >= since
638	                     and (until is None or message["received_at"] < until)]
639	            # A ticket without a selected follow-up takes no part in the query.
640	            if not pairs:
641	                continue
642	            response = ticket.get("first_response")
643	            # Missing, null or an empty object means there is no first response;
644	            # handwritten and knowledge answers are collected the same way. The
645	            # answer set ignores the window: an answer outside it may still cover
646	            # a selected follow-up.
647	            times = [response["responded_at"]] if isinstance(response, dict) and response else []
648	            times.extend(reply["replied_at"] for reply in ticket.get("replies") or [])
649	            # A selected follow-up, or any answer of the same ticket, later than
650	            # as_of invalidates the whole query; follow-ups outside the window
651	            # and tickets without a selected follow-up are never checked.
652	            if any(message["received_at"] > as_of for _, message in pairs) or \
653	                    any(time > as_of for time in times):
654	                raise ValueError("customer message or response time must not be later than as_of")
655	            answers[ticket["ticket_id"]] = times
656	            windowed[ticket["ticket_id"]] = pairs
657	        items = []
658	        for ticket in participants:
659	            ticket_id = ticket["ticket_id"]
660	            pairs = windowed.get(ticket_id)
661	            if not pairs:
662	                continue
663	            for index, message in pairs:
664	                received_at = message["received_at"]
665	                # Matching looks at time only: the earliest answer not earlier than
666	                # the follow-up covers it, regardless of call order or window bounds;
667	                # the same answer may cover several follow-ups and equal times take
668	                # zero minutes.
669	                candidates = [time for time in answers[ticket_id] if time >= received_at]
670	                if candidates:
671	                    answered_at = min(candidates)
672	                    items.append({"ticket_id": ticket_id, "index": index,
673	                                  "received_at": received_at, "answered_at": answered_at,
674	                                  "response_minutes": answered_at - received_at,
675	                                  "outcome": "answered"})
676	                else:
677	                    outcome = "pending" if ticket["status"] != "closed" else "closed_without_answer"
678	                    items.append({"ticket_id": ticket_id, "index": index,
679	                                  "received_at": received_at, "answered_at": None,
680	                                  "response_minutes": None, "outcome": outcome})
681	        items.sort(key=lambda item: (item["received_at"], item["ticket_id"], item["index"]))
682	        durations = [item["response_minutes"] for item in items if item["outcome"] == "answered"]
683	        summary = {
684	            "total": len(items),
685	            "answered": sum(1 for item in items if item["outcome"] == "answered"),
686	            "pending": sum(1 for item in items if item["outcome"] == "pending"),
687	            "closed_without_answer": sum(1 for item in items
688	                                         if item["outcome"] == "closed_without_answer"),
689	            "average_minutes": sum(durations) / len(durations) if durations else None,
690	            "max_minutes": max(durations) if durations else None,
691	        }
692	        return {"as_of": as_of, "summary": summary, "items": items}

1203	        normalized = []
1204	        for rule in rules:

1207	            category = rule["category"]
1208	            if not isinstance(category, str) or not category.strip():
1209	                raise ValueError("rule category must be a nonblank string")
1210	            query = rule["query"]
1211	            if not isinstance(query, str) or not query.strip():
1212	                raise ValueError("rule query must be a nonblank string")
1213	            # Queries split on whitespace and fold case; punctuation stays part of
1214	            # the token and matches literally. Several rules may share a category.
1215	            normalized.append((category.strip(),
1216	                               [term.casefold() for term in query.strip().split()]))
1217	        data = self._read()
1218	        candidates = [ticket for ticket in data.get("tickets", {}).values()
1219	                      if ticket["status"] == "open" and ticket.get("category") is None]
1220	        classified = []

1226	            haystacks = [ticket["subject"].casefold()]
1227	            haystacks.extend(message["message"].casefold()
1228	                             for message in ticket.get("customer_messages") or [])
1229	            chosen = None
1230	            # Rule order decides priority; the first matching rule wins.

import json
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from support_desk import SupportDesk

class ProductTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.temp.cleanup)
        self.root = Path(self.temp.name)
        self.app = SupportDesk(self.root)

    def test_assignment_note_closure_and_reopen(self):
        self.app.open_ticket("T", "Alice", "Download")
        self.app.assign("T", "Bob")
        self.app.note("T", "Checked")
        self.app.close("T", "Sent link")
        value = SupportDesk(self.root).get("T")
        self.assertEqual((value["status"], value["notes"]), ("closed", ["Checked"]))

    def test_unassigned_and_empty_resolution_cannot_close(self):
        self.app.open_ticket("T", "Alice", "Download")
        before = self.app.path.read_bytes()
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.app.close("T", "Sent link")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.app.close("T", " ")
        self.assertEqual(before, self.app.path.read_bytes())

    def test_closed_ticket_is_not_mutated_and_filter_works(self):
        self.app.open_ticket("T", "Alice", "Download")
        self.app.assign("T", "Bob")
        self.app.close("T", "Done")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.app.note("T", "Late")
        self.assertEqual(self.app.list_tickets("open"), [])

    def test_cli_demo_and_invalid_action(self):
        result = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "support_desk", "--root", str(self.root), "demo"], text=True, capture_output=True)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        value = json.loads(result.stdout)
        self.assertEqual((value["status"], value["assignee"]), ("closed", "小林"))
        failed = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "support_desk", "--root", str(self.root), "not-an-action"], text=True, capture_output=True)
        self.assertEqual(failed.returncode, 2)

    def test_response_queue_waits_and_overdue_boundary(self):
        self.app.open_ticket("T-9", "Alice", "A", opened_at=9)
        self.app.open_ticket("T-10", "Bob", "B", opened_at=10)
        self.app.open_ticket("T-40", "Cara", "C", opened_at=40)
        queue = self.app.response_queue(40)
        self.assertEqual(queue["untimed"], 0)
        self.assertEqual([(i["ticket"]["ticket_id"], i["waiting_minutes"], i["overdue"]) for i in queue["items"]],
                         [("T-9", 31, True), ("T-10", 30, False), ("T-40", 0, False)])
        self.assertEqual(queue["items"][0]["ticket"], self.app.get("T-9"))

    def test_response_queue_skips_closed_responded_and_counts_untimed(self):
        self.app.open_ticket("T-open", "Alice", "A", opened_at=5)
        self.app.open_ticket("T-untimed", "Bob", "B")
        self.app.open_ticket("T-responded", "Cara", "C", opened_at=5)
        self.app.respond("T-responded", "On it", 6)
        self.app.open_ticket("T-closed", "Dan", "D", opened_at=5)

    def test_reply_blocked_when_closed_and_reopen_keeps_history_and_time_order(self):
        ticket_id = self._reply_scenario()
        self.app.assign(ticket_id, "Bob")
        self.app.reply(ticket_id, "Before close", 7)
        self.app.reply_with_knowledge(ticket_id, "KB-1", 8)
        self.app.close(ticket_id, "Resolved")
        before = self.app.path.read_bytes()
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.app.reply(ticket_id, "Late", 9)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.app.reply_with_knowledge(ticket_id, "KB-1", 9)
        self.assertEqual(before, self.app.path.read_bytes())
        self.app.reopen_ticket(ticket_id, "regression")
        ticket = self.app.get(ticket_id)
        self.assertEqual([(r["message"], r["replied_at"]) for r in ticket["replies"]],
                         [("Before close", 7), ("Sent link", 8)])
        # the original chronology still bounds new replies
        for replied_at in (5, 7):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError, msg=replied_at):
                self.app.reply(ticket_id, "Too early", replied_at)
        ticket = self.app.reply(ticket_id, "After reopen", 9)
        self.assertEqual([r["replied_at"] for r in ticket["replies"]], [7, 8, 9])

def test_response_target_report_normal_counts_group_order_and_recreation(self):
        self._response_report_scenario()
        report = self.app.response_target_report(100)
        self.assertEqual(report["as_of"], 100)
        self.assertEqual([g["priority"] for g in report["groups"]],
                         ["urgent", "high", "normal", "low"])
        normal = self._report_groups(report)["normal"]
        self.assertEqual(normal["target_minutes"], 30)
        self.assertEqual((normal["responded"], normal["on_time"], normal["late"],
                          normal["pending"], normal["overdue"], normal["untimed"],
                          normal["closed_without_response"]), (2, 1, 1, 2, 1, 1, 1))
        self.assertEqual(normal["on_time_rate"], 0.5)
        for name in ("urgent", "high", "low"):
            group = self._report_groups(report)[name]
            self.assertEqual((group["responded"], group["on_time"], group["late"],
                              group["pending"], group["overdue"], group["untimed"],
                              group["closed_without_response"]), (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0))
            self.assertIsNone(group["on_time_rate"])
        # recreating SupportDesk in the same directory gives the same report
        recreated = SupportDesk(self.root).response_target_report(100)
        self.assertEqual(recreated, report)
        # read-only: no backfilled priority or clock fields, unchanged bytes
        self.assertNotIn("priority", self.app.get("T-pending-30"))
        self.assertNotIn("opened_at", self.app.get("T-untimed-closed"))
        before = self.app.path.read_bytes()
        self.app.response_target_report(100)
        self.assertEqual(before, self.app.path.read_bytes())

    def test_response_target_report_override_normal_target_to_31(self):
        self._response_report_scenario()
        report = self.app.response_target_report(100, {"normal": 31})
        groups = self._report_groups(report)
        # uncovered priorities keep their default targets
        self.assertEqual([groups[name]["target_minutes"] for name in ("urgent", "high", "normal", "low")],
                         [5, 15, 31, 60])
        normal = groups["normal"]
        self.assertEqual((normal["responded"], normal["on_time"], normal["late"],
                          normal["pending"], normal["overdue"], normal["untimed"],
                          normal["closed_without_response"]), (2, 2, 0, 2, 0, 1, 1))
        self.assertEqual(normal["on_time_rate"], 1.0)

    def test_response_target_report_omitted_null_and_empty_targets_use_defaults(self):
        self._response_report_scenario()
        omitted = self.app.response_target_report(100)
        self.assertEqual(self.app.response_target_report(100, None), omitted)
        self.assertEqual(self.app.response_target_report(100, {}), omitted)
        self.assertEqual([g["target_minutes"] for g in omitted["groups"]], [5, 15, 30, 60])

    def test_response_target_report_old_tickets_default_to_normal_without_backfill(self):
        self.app.open_ticket("T-old", "Alice", "Old", opened_at=70)
        self.app.open_ticket("T-urgent", "Bob", "U", opened_at=0)
        self.app.set_priority("T-urgent", "urgent")
        self.app.respond("T-urgent", "Seen", 10)
        groups = self._report_groups(self.app.response_target_report(100))
        self.assertEqual((groups["urgent"]["responded"], groups["urgent"]["on_time"],
                          groups["urgent"]["late"], groups["urgent"]["on_time_rate"]),
                         (1, 0, 1, 0.0))
        # 30-minute wait against the 30-minute normal target is not overdue
        self.assertEqual((groups["normal"]["pending"], groups["normal"]["overdue"]), (1, 0))
        self.assertNotIn("priority", self.app.get("T-old"))
